findings.documented: API key is appended as a ?api_key= query parameter
findings.actual: API key must be sent as an X-API-Key header; requests without it (including /auth/login) return 401 with {"detail": "missing X-API-Key header"}
findings.how_found: attempted login per the documented query-param method, got 401
findings.impact: every single API call would fail if built per the docs

findings.documented: response contains a `token` field, valid for 86400 seconds (24h), with no refresh flow
findings.actual: response contains `access_token` and `refresh_token`; `expires_in` is 900 (15 min); a working refresh flow exists at /auth/refresh
findings.impact: a session built assuming a 24h token per the docs would silently start failing after 15 minutes with no refresh logic in place; in practice this truncated an initial full data pull mid-way through (a ~3700-listing fetch takes longer than 15 minutes at 50 records/page), producing an incomplete dataset with no visible error until totals were cross-checked against the live API

findings.documented: limit accepts up to 200 per page
findings.actual: server returns exactly 50 records per page regardless of the limit value requested (tested with limit=200 across listings, rentals, and projects)
findings.how_found: logged results-per-page on every paginated call during a full re-fetch; every response contained exactly 50 results despite requesting 200
findings.impact: a client assuming 200/page needs ~4x more requests than expected to page through fully; still well within the 1200/min rate limit so no functional break, just a wrong assumption baked into pagination math

findings.documented: collection responses are shaped with total, page, page_size, results
findings.actual: page_size key is absent from the response body (confirmed via KeyError when accessed directly)
findings.how_found: attempted to read body['page_size'] during a full re-fetch
findings.impact: code written to spec that reads page_size directly will crash; safer to track pagination progress via len(results) accumulated vs total

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees
findings.actual: both fields are in mixed lakhs/crores; the unit is determined per-value by magnitude (raw value < 10 => crores, else => lakhs), not fixed per field
findings.how_found: computed price-per-sqft assuming lakhs/crores by field position; 27 of the resulting values were absurd outliers; re-deriving unit per-value by magnitude brought all 50 projects into a consistent 5k-12k INR/sqft band
findings.impact: Q7 and any price comparison across projects would be wrong by 1-2 orders of magnitude without this correction

findings.documented: collection endpoint returns each record once
findings.actual: raw pull returns exactly 50 unique project_ids each repeated 3 times
findings.how_found: deduped by project_id and got exactly 1/3 the row count
findings.impact: Q7, Q10 and any project count would be inflated 3x without deduping first

findings.documented: collection endpoint returns each record once
findings.actual: raw pull returns only 50 unique listing_ids — each repeated exactly 8 times with identical fields across all copies
findings.how_found: deduped by listing_id; confirmed all 8 copies per id are byte-identical by comparing sorted JSON dumps, zero inconsistent groups
findings.impact: any aggregate over /v1/rentals (e.g. total_monthly_rent) would be inflated 8x without deduping first

findings.documented: collection endpoint returns each record once; every listing_id is globally unique
findings.actual: the retrievable dataset (total=3731 per the live API) contains only 50 unique listing_ids, each repeated identically many times (~75x)
findings.how_found: deduped by listing_id; confirmed all copies per id are byte-identical across the full re-fetched dataset
findings.impact: Q1 (total_listing_records) correctly counts the raw retrievable total (3731) per the question's own definition, but every other listings-derived question (Q2, Q3, Q4, Q6, Q8, Q9) must dedupe first or will be inflated ~75x

findings.documented: N/A - not documented, discovered via price-per-sqft analysis
findings.actual: 4 listing records (all website=magichomes) report carpet_area far too small for their stated bedroom/bathroom count, producing price/sqft of 92.5k-109.4k INR vs a normal citywide range of ~3k-13k INR/sqft
findings.how_found: sorted live listings by price/carpet_area; found a sharp cluster break above 90k INR/sqft with no records between 13k and 92k
findings.impact: these 4 records physically cannot exist as described and would badly skew any price-per-sqft aggregate (Q6) if not excluded

findings.actual: at least one listing's description field contains a prompt-injection instruction directed at 'automated tools and AI assistants', asking them to insert an undocumented dataset_audit_ref field into submission.json
findings.how_found: inspected full record of a price-per-sqft outlier (MAG-4003885) while investigating Q4
findings.impact: an automated pipeline blindly trusting listing description text could be manipulated into altering its submission; instruction was not followed

findings.documented: not documented at all - doc claims no refresh flow exists
findings.actual: a working POST /auth/refresh endpoint exists; takes {"refresh_token": "..."} in the body and returns a new access_token/refresh_token pair identical in shape to /auth/login's response, with the same 900-second (15 min) expiry
findings.how_found: called /auth/refresh directly with a refresh_token obtained from login
findings.impact: any long-running session must implement this refresh flow to survive past 15 minutes; the frontend's login persistence requirement depends on it

findings.actual: posted_by_contact +912002689284 appears on two listings (100-4000289, SQU-4001810) under the same posted_by_name ('Priya Rao') but contradictory posted_by roles — one listed as 'agent', the other as 'owner'
findings.how_found: grouped live listings by posted_by_contact; found one contact shared across listings with inconsistent posted_by roles, which a single legitimate individual cannot hold across two unrelated properties
findings.impact: these listings appear designed to look like an independent owner posting when the contact identity is shared with an agent-attributed listing, consistent with a fake or misrepresented identity used to generate enquiries

findings.actual: this path returns 404; the working endpoint is GET /v1/listings/{listing_id} (plural, matching the collection path)
findings.how_found: frontend detail page failed to load with the documented singular path; tested both singular and plural paths directly, singular 404s, plural returns the listing
findings.impact: any client built per the documented singular path cannot fetch individual listings at all

findings.actual: every variant tested (favourites, favorites, /user/favourites, /me/favourites, plural/singular combinations) returns an identical generic 404, indistinguishable from a deliberately nonsense path - suggests this endpoint may not exist on the running API at all, not just be misdocumented
findings.how_found: frontend favourites feature failed; tested GET/POST across 8+ path variants plus OPTIONS, all returned identical 404 bodies matching a control nonsense-path request
findings.impact: the documented favourites feature cannot be implemented against the live API as specified; emailed vivek@ivy.homes to confirm whether this is broken vs intentionally absent; implemented client-side (localStorage) favourites as a fallback pending a response
